overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting a March 5 notice implying no open session would precede executive session, but did not violate it by discussing OML complaints in executive session under Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee convened executive session before meeting in open session on March 5; the notice's order of business suggested no open session came first.
allegations.key_passage: we find the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting a notice that gave the impression that there would be no open session prior to the executive session during which the public could witness the procedure to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that discussing Open Meeting Law complaints about the committee itself in executive session under Purpose 1 was improper and should have been held in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it discussed three Open Meeting Law complaints in executive session during its March 5 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Law and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
